name: The long way up
about: From the glide to the Window, outside in: the order a visitor meets Sorrel.

stops.note: You arrive the way almost everyone does: 140 seconds of free fall from Lovage, through a dark hall that would kill you, behind a metre of water.
The catch. A cradle on the quay takes the car on a soft arm and brings a full g back over a second or two.
In through the jacket: fifty metres of liquid hydrogen at 20 K, crossed in about a minute in the dark.
Old Three, the busiest blocks in Sorrel. Everything from Lovage and Tansy comes through here.
Anything alive stops here first. In a drum fed by monoculture vats, a stray phage is a famine.
Two Rings along the Keel the food plant begins, and so does the air you'll breathe in a few months' time.
Every Ring has one. In Sorrel you go up to retire and down to die, and the dead come home to the cycles.
Into the Lattice. Ask for the long way round and a cab will carry you spinward at 1.2 g.
Seventy decks up, the Low decks, where Sorrel raises its children near full weight.
Spinball, two decks tall. Axis flies true, spin sinks, anti floats.
Mid-drum at 0.73 g: one street that runs right round the deck and meets itself.
Twenty-three thousand years of every place, every heir and every name.
The High decks begin. This is where Sorrel's old go up.
The last stair, beside the jetty's pavilion core.
Out through the ground into the Hollow. Look up: the far bank is three kilometres overhead, upside down.
The back wall, climbing toward the axis, lighter with every tier.
Down swings sideways, then toward the axis, then fades to nothing.
Nothing boils at the axis, so the tea comes up by lift in lidded bulbs.
Heat out: a river of ammonia through the great joint. The loudest place in Sorrel.
Here you let go of Sorrel's turn and step into the part of the raft where nothing turns.
Twenty minutes of red light, and then the shutter. Every Sorrel child comes once, at about eight.

name: A life in Sorrel
about: One life, about 120 years, told in seventeen places.

stops.note: Day one. Proofread before you were born, and caught at nearly a full g, near the Low decks' schools.
A week old. You're named for someone whose place you now hold, and their family comes to see.
Every year, measured at near full weight, because every parent in Sorrel believes it matters.
Toys on loan, mended between children. New mass is dear.
School on the Low decks, and spinball at break.
Eight. The River, once, with one adult of your choosing.
Fifteen, and your first time going dark: a black thread round the left wrist means don't message me, I won't see it.
Twenty, and the slow line to anywhere: a kay a leg, weeks aboard, and a card home from every row.
Married at a third of a g, at dusk, with an apple cut crosswise to show the star.
Your grandparents' sofa, remade. A new one would cost forty-six days of a wallet.
Two birth rights, spent: one for each place, given but never sold.
Fifty years of work, give or take, in one of a thousand trades. Most of them mend something.
About a hundred, and you go up.
The lake every morning at lamp-dawn, in order of age.
The last rooms, two decks below the lake.
And down.
Your place goes back to the pool. Before long, a child somewhere in Sorrel carries your name.

name: The Daces' Sorrel
about: Four days with the Dace family, in the places they go.

stops.note: The Daces' flat is on deck 77, off Pear Street, two corners from the Court.
The Court, and the light vote it has won six times running, mostly because of the pears.
Teo goes down 76 decks in about thirty seconds to the Gate at Station Ring Three.
Anselm opens Dace's: coats relined, trousers let out, a sofa remade for about a fifth of the price of new.
Ossian at spinball. He's small, and throws anti.
Wren and the dark kids, black threads on their wrists, in the warmest room in Ashgrove.
Up 284 decks to Hedda's, losing 40% of their weight on the way.
Fifteen decks more, and up through the ground among apple trees.
Hedda on the bench, Teo in the lake, Anselm asleep with his jacket over his eyes.
Wren flies for an hour without thinking about anything at all.
To Lovage for Mira's wedding, with a chair in a padded bag and two bottles of gin each.
Ossian and his grandmother, and the River.

name: Lamp-night
about: Sorrel after the sunline goes out, from dusk to the plain dawn.

stops.note: Dusk. The low lamps come on round the back Dim End.
The sunline falls below a seventh of full, and the whole axis opens for flying.
The spar crews go out at seven, with an amber lamp, to the line nobody can look at by day.
After nine the water goes back out to the moat through the turbines, and couples sit to hear it.
The last train to Lovage leaves at one. Noodles until it's gone.
Laundry at the night price, and jook at four for elders who sleep in pieces.
The night crews' canteen. Breakfast from midnight.
Tomorrow's goods, packed into carts by lobby while the drum sleeps.
Six o'clock. Sorrel's dawn, plain, warm and then white, because painted dawns are for show.
